name_en: Laos Ancient Tree Sun-dried Black Tea

brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A sun-dried black tea from large-leaf old trees in Phongsaly Province, northern Laos, next to Xishuangbanna in Yunnan.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: The area lies at 1,200 to 1,800 metres, and the unpruned trees are described as often over a hundred years old, some 300 to 400. Little more is documented about it.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Large, thick, intact dark brown leaves with golden tips.
taste_profile: Honey and fruit first, then caramel, red date and chocolate-like sweetness over light wood; thick, long and low in astringency, holding up over many infusions.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
